findings.reason: implementing §2 as written breaks the cited method, while following §8 produces a different import structure in the produced module, so the plan must say which governs rather than leave the worker with two contradictory authorities.
findings.text: §2 states "The import runs one way at module level. `reckon/pace_report.py` imports `reckon.budget`", but §8 of `every-module-fits-a-worker-window`, which line 37 cites as the method this split follows, states "A produced module never imports the original at module level. An unavoidable back-reference uses the function-level import this codebase already uses for cycles"

findings.reason: the misnamed owner moves nothing, since the helpers still land in `pace_report.py` and the worker resolves the real import from the source, so only the rationale sentence is wrong.
findings.text: §2 says "The lift-reading helpers read the lift lifecycle that `reckon/crew/lift_watch.py` owns"; at `76946f9a9` the helpers read `reckon.crew.budget_lift` (`budget.py:3495-3510`: `budget_lift.SESSION_PREFIX`, `budget_lift.list_lifts`, `budget_lift.effective_budget`), `budget.py` never references `lift_watch`, and `lift_watch.py`'s own docstring names `budget_lift.end_cause` as the resolver it reads through

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `f5e88d284`, `76946f9a9` and `6ebe65ba4` resolve and are ancestors of HEAD; `reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:113` carries `DEFAULT_CREDIT_RESERVE_FRACTION` with its comment; the extensionless sibling link resolves as `every-module-fits-a-worker-window.html` and its §8 resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2 names a measurable bound (`tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py` no longer names `reckon/budget.py`, at most 45,000 tokens, `pace_report.py` and `budget_lift.py` at most 40,000) and a declared negative control: revert `budget.py` to its base content and the width test names it again.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the plan places no evidence in a scratch or node-local path; the gate logs land on the run's own evidence directory under the dispatch contract.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `reckon/pace_report.py` names the capability it adds, and no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol or a comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — §2's stated import direction contradicts §8 of the method it cites, and §2 attributes the lift lifecycle to `lift_watch.py` rather than to `budget_lift.py`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one deliverable, moving the pace and lift family out of `budget.py`; §1 is the done why.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` names `{"s2":["lane-and-model-routing#s46"]}` and `plan-informs` names `lane-and-model-routing`, and lane-and-model-routing's own `s48` declares `["lane-and-model-routing#s46","budget-fits-a-worker-window#s2"]`, which is what §2 line 73 asserts.
